title: Global Molecular Epidemiology and Genotype-Phenotype Correlations in Keratinocytic Epidermal Nevus: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Keratinocytic epidermal nevi (KEN) represent a heterogeneous group of mosaic skin disorders driven by diverse causative genes. This systematic review aimed to delineate the global molecular epidemiology of KEN, establish genotype-phenotype correlations, and define a stratified framework for molecular diagnosis and targeted therapy. We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to May 31, 2026. Data from 141 patients across 77 reports were extracted, and associations were analyzed by histopathological subtype, lesion distribution, and systemic involvement. Generalized KEN was more common than localized forms (55.3% vs. 36.2%). Pathogenic mutations were detected in 79.4% of cases, most frequently in HRAS, KRT10, FGFR3, KRAS, and FGFR2. Non-epidermolytic KEN (n = 94) predominantly harbored RAS/MAPK and receptor tyrosine kinase pathway mutations, whereas epidermolytic KEN (n = 18) was associated with KRT1/2/10 mutations, and inflammatory linear verrucous epidermal nevus (n = 24) displayed heterogeneous alterations. Mutation detection in lesional skin was significantly higher than in peripheral blood (78.3% vs. 27.8%), with generalized forms showing higher peripheral blood positivity than localized forms (41.0% versus 14.0%). HRAS c.34G>A and FGFR3 c.742C>T were predominantly observed in generalized KEN, whereas HRAS c.37G>C, FGFR2 c.755C>G, and EGFR exon 20 insertions were mainly detected in localized disease. Extracutaneous manifestations (27.7% of cases, primarily with KRAS, FGFR3, and HRAS) and parent-to-offspring transmission (15 pedigrees, predominantly involving KRT1/10) more often occurred in generalized KEN. Nine patients received genotype-directed targeted therapies with satisfactory responses. These findings delineate a comprehensive genotype-phenotype landscape of KEN and propose a lesional tissue-based tiered molecular diagnostic strategy incorporating high-depth sequencing for mechanism-driven targeted therapy and genetic counseling. Integrating clinical, histopathological, and molecular data within this framework offers a practical foundation for diagnostic stratification and precision medicine in KEN.

title: RSV Molecular Epidemiology Pre- and Post-COVID-19 Pandemic Periods in Seattle, Washington, USA.
abstract: Globally, RSV declined to historically low levels following stay-at-home orders in 2020 and re-emerged as restrictions lifted, with large inter-seasonal outbreaks and other shifts in epidemiology. The effect of the pandemic restrictions on genomic diversity has not been well studied. Individuals with respiratory symptoms were enrolled into community-based surveillance studies and provided nasal swabs over three respiratory virus seasons from 2019 to 2022 in the Seattle metropolitan area in Washington State, USA. Samples were tested for RSV by RT-qPCR, with whole genome sequencing performed for a subset. Among children and adults, respectively, 1.8% (232/13,014) and 0.2% (86/46,042) of samples tested positive for RSV-A and 1.1% (139/13016) and 0.3% (119/46043) for RSV-B. Positive cases were observed in childcare (n = 39), clinic (n = 270), university (n = 20), workplace (n = 32) or nursing facility (n = 1) sites and through at-home self-administered testing (n = 253). Median age for all participants was 33 years (IQR: 23, 48) and 3 years (IQR: 3, 33) for those who tested positive. Cough (≥ 85%) and rhinorrhea (≥ 85%) were the most common symptoms for RSV cases. During 2019-2020, six RSV-A and three RSV-B lineages circulated (majority lineages A.D.1 and B.D.4.1.1). Almost no RSV was detected during 2020-2021. During 2021-2022, RSV-B lineage B.D.E.1 was dominant. In a community surveillance study spanning several years, RSV was commonly detected in young children across several sites. Circulation of RSV was disrupted by pandemic mitigation measures, with shifts in genomic diversity detected after lifting of pandemic restrictions.

title: Molecular epidemiology of NDM-producing Enterobacterales in Huai'an, China: Genomic diversity and evaluation of aztreonam-avibactam and cefiderocol.
abstract: Metallo-β-lactamase-producing carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (MBL-CRE) pose a serious threat due to antimicrobial resistance. However, their prevalence in the Huai'an region of Jiangsu Province in eastern China remains unknown. Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) isolates collected from Xuyi People's Hospital were screened for carbapenemase production using the modified carbapenem inactivation method (mCIM) and EDTA-modified carbapenem inactivation method (eCIM), followed by PCR confirmation. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, biofilm formation assays, growth kinetics analyses, and whole-genome sequencing with bioinformatics were performed to characterize the isolates. The 12 NDM-producing Enterobacterales identified comprised seven Escherichia coli, three Klebsiella pneumoniae, and two Enterobacter hormaechei. Beyond carbapenem resistance, resistance to aztreonam, tetracycline, fluoroquinolones, and aminoglycosides was common among the isolates. Four isolates (including three E. coli) showed intermediate susceptibility to cefiderocol, and the aztreonam-avibactam combination exhibited synergistic activity against aztreonam-resistant Enterobacteriaceae isolates. Genomic analysis revealed eight isolates carrying blaNDM-5, three carrying blaNDM-1, and one carrying blaNDM-13. All isolates belonged to distinct sequence types, including two novel types. The NDM-13 isolate and one NDM-1-positive E. hormaechei isolate displayed distinct genetic contexts, whereas most isolates harbored a blaNDM-bleMBL-trpF-tat-dct genetic structure. Among the three cefiderocol-intermediate E. coli isolates, mutations were identified in cirA and ftsI. This study reveals the prevalence and diverse genetic backgrounds of MBL-CRE in Xuyi County, demonstrates the potent activity of aztreonam-avibactam, and suggests that cefiderocol resistance may involve multiple factors.
